title: Modules of finite presentation are quasi-coherent; a quasi-coherent module is of finite type (finite presentation) on an affine open iff its sections there are a finite (finitely presented) module (Stacks 01BO, 01PB, 01PC)
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. (0) Every $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite presentation (defined below) is quasi-coherent. Now let $\mathcal F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module [pqf-def-coherent], [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. An $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ is *of finite presentation* if every point of $X$ has an open neighbourhood $U$ with an exact sequence $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G|_U\to0$ of $\mathcal O_U$-modules (Stacks, Modules, Definition 01BN). Let $U\subseteq X$ be an affine open and $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$. Then (a) $\mathcal F|_U$ is of finite type [pqf-def-coherent] if and only if $\mathcal F(U)$ is a finitely generated $R$-module; (b) $\mathcal F|_U$ is of finite presentation if and only if $\mathcal F(U)$ is a finitely presented $R$-module (one isomorphic to $R^{n}/K$ for some $n\ge0$ and some finitely generated submodule $K\subseteq R^n$, equivalently the cokernel of an $R$-linear map $R^m\to R^n$). Consequently (c) if $X=\bigcup_jU_j$ is an affine open covering with $\mathcal F(U_j)$ finitely generated over $\mathcal O_X(U_j)$ for all $j$, then $\mathcal F$ is of finite type and $\mathcal F(U)$ is a finitely generated $\mathcal O_X(U)$-module for every affine open $U\subseteq X$; and if $\mathcal F$ is of finite presentation then $\mathcal F(U)$ is a finitely presented $\mathcal O_X(U)$-module for every affine open $U$.

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BO (lemma-finite-presentation-quasi-coherent, modules.tex line 1421) for (0); Properties, Lemma 01PB (lemma-finite-type-module, line 2093) and Lemma 01PC (lemma-finite-presentation-module, line 2113); (c) because finite type and finite presentation are local properties (Modules, Definitions 01B5 and 01BN)

proof.text: *Step 1 (setup on an affine open; maps out of free modules).* Let $U\subseteq X$ be an affine open and $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$. Since $U$ is an affine scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}R,\mathcal O)=R$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], there is an isomorphism $\operatorname{Spec}R\cong U$ inducing the identity on global sections, and composing with the inclusion an open immersion $g:X_U:=\operatorname{Spec}R\to X$ with image $U$. For an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$, the restriction $\mathcal G|_{X_U}$ along $g$ is $\mathcal G|_U$ transported along $X_U\cong U$, with $\Gamma(X_U,\mathcal G|_{X_U})=\mathcal G(U)$ as $R$-modules, and it is quasi-coherent if $\mathcal G$ is [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits](2); being of finite type or of finite presentation is invariant under isomorphisms of ringed spaces and of modules, so these properties of $\mathcal G|_U$ and of $\mathcal G|_{X_U}$ agree. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-tilde-free-module], transported along $g$, $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}$ is quasi-coherent with $\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n})=R^n$, the basis sections $e_i$ being the standard basis. For any open $W$ and any $\mathcal O_W$-module $\mathcal G$, an $\mathcal O_W$-linear $\varphi:\mathcal O_W^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G$ is determined by the sections $s_i=\varphi_W(e_i)\in\mathcal G(W)$, since on $V\subseteq W$ every section of $\mathcal O_W^{\oplus n}$ is $\sum_if_ie_i|_V$ and $\varphi_V(\sum f_ie_i|_V)=\sum_if_is_i|_V$ by linearity and compatibility with restriction; conversely every $(s_1,\dots,s_n)$ defines such a $\varphi_s$ by this formula [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. On $W$-sections $\varphi_{s,W}$ is the map $\mathcal O(W)^n\to\mathcal G(W)$, $e_i\mapsto s_i$, and $\varphi_s$ is surjective as a map of sheaves exactly when $s_1,\dots,s_n$ generate $\mathcal G$ [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections]. So $\mathcal G$ is of finite type [pqf-def-coherent] iff every point has an open neighbourhood $W$ such that $\mathcal G|_W$ is generated by finitely many sections over $W$ (this is how Stacks reads Definition 01B5).

source.place: Modules, Definition 01B5 and the paragraph after it; Properties, Section 'Characterizing modules of finite type and finite presentation' (the identification of an affine open with Spec of its sections)

proof.text: *Step 2 (two facts on an affine open).* Let $U$, $R$, $g$ be as in Step 1. (i) A morphism $\alpha:\mathcal G\to\mathcal G'$ of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-modules such that $\alpha_U:\mathcal G(U)\to\mathcal G'(U)$ is bijective is an isomorphism. Indeed, transported to $X_U=\operatorname{Spec}R$, the counits $\varepsilon_{\mathcal G}:\widetilde{\mathcal G(U)}\to\mathcal G$ and $\varepsilon_{\mathcal G'}$ are isomorphisms [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](3) and natural, $\alpha\circ\varepsilon_{\mathcal G}=\varepsilon_{\mathcal G'}\circ\widetilde{\alpha_U}$ (naturality of the adjunction (1)); $\widetilde{\alpha_U}$ is an isomorphism since $\alpha_U$ is and $M\mapsto\widetilde M$ is a functor; hence $\alpha=\varepsilon_{\mathcal G'}\widetilde{\alpha_U}\varepsilon_{\mathcal G}^{-1}$ is an isomorphism. (ii) In particular (take $\mathcal G'=0$) a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-module with $\mathcal G(U)=0$ is zero. (Stacks: Schemes 01IB, quasi-coherent modules on $\operatorname{Spec}R$ are equivalent to $R$-modules via $\Gamma$.)

*Step 3 (generation by sections over an affine open).* Let $\mathcal G$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module, $U\subseteq X$ an affine open, $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$ and $s_1,\dots,s_n\in\mathcal G(U)$. Then $s_1,\dots,s_n$ generate $\mathcal G|_U$ [def-weil-pbc-generating-sections] if and only if $\mathcal G(U)=\sum_iRs_i$. Proof: let $\varphi=\varphi_s:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal G|_U$ (Step 1), a morphism of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_U$-modules (Step 1 for both), with $\varphi_U(R^n)=\sum_iRs_i$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] to the scheme $U$ and $\varphi$: with $q:\mathcal G|_U\to\operatorname{Coker}\varphi$, (1) $\operatorname{Im}\varphi=\ker q$, (2) $\operatorname{Coker}\varphi$ is quasi-coherent, (3) for the affine open $U$: $(\operatorname{Im}\varphi)(U)=\varphi_U(R^n)$ and $(\operatorname{Coker}\varphi)(U)=\mathcal G(U)/\varphi_U(R^n)$. If the $s_i$ generate, $\varphi$ is surjective, i.e. $\operatorname{Im}\varphi=\mathcal G|_U$, so $\mathcal G(U)=(\operatorname{Im}\varphi)(U)=\sum_iRs_i$ by (3). Conversely if $\mathcal G(U)=\sum_iRs_i$ then $(\operatorname{Coker}\varphi)(U)=0$, so $\operatorname{Coker}\varphi=0$ by Step 2(ii) and (2); then $q=0$, $\operatorname{Im}\varphi=\ker q=\mathcal G|_U$ by (1), i.e. $\varphi$ is surjective and the $s_i$ generate. (This is the step 'Thus $M_{f_i}$ is finitely generated' of Stacks 01PB and the converse that Stacks leaves implicit; the finiteness half is the sorry-free slopmaster2 declaration AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.Modules.finite_sections_top_of_isIso_fromTildeΓ.)

source.place: Properties, proof of Lemma 01PB (lemma-finite-type-module), sentence 'Thus M_{f_i} is finitely generated for each i'; Schemes, Lemma 01IC (lemma-kernel-cokernel-quasi-coherent)

proof.text: *Step 4 (part (0): finite presentation implies quasi-coherent).* Let $\mathcal G$ be an $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite presentation and $x\in X$. Choose an open $W\ni x$ and an exact sequence $\mathcal O_W^{\oplus m}\xrightarrow{\chi}\mathcal O_W^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\pi}\mathcal G|_W\to0$, and an affine open $V$ with $x\in V\subseteq W$ (the open subscheme $W$ is a scheme, so $x$ has an affine open neighbourhood in it [def-pc-scheme]). Restriction to the open $V$ preserves colimits, in particular cokernels [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits](1) (a cokernel is a colimit [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]), so $\mathcal G|_V\cong\operatorname{Coker}(\chi|_V)$, where $\chi|_V:\mathcal O_V^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_V^{\oplus n}$ is a morphism of quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_V$-modules (Step 1 applied to the scheme $V$, affine open of itself). By [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image](2) (on the scheme $V$) $\operatorname{Coker}(\chi|_V)$, hence $\mathcal G|_V$, is quasi-coherent. So by the definition [pqf-def-coherent] applied to $\mathcal G|_V$ at $x$ there is an affine neighbourhood $V'\subseteq V$ of $x$ with $\mathcal G|_{V'}\cong\widetilde M$; as $x$ was arbitrary, $\mathcal G$ is quasi-coherent. (Stacks proves 01BO 'immediately from the definitions' because Stacks defines quasi-coherence (Modules 01BD) by local presentations $\bigoplus_J\mathcal O\to\bigoplus_I\mathcal O\to\mathcal F\to0$; with the definition of [pqf-def-coherent] ($\mathcal F|_U\cong\widetilde M$) the step through the cokernel lemma is needed.)

source.place: Modules, Lemma 01BO (lemma-finite-presentation-quasi-coherent), line 1421, and Definition 01BD (quasi-coherent); Schemes, Lemma 01IC

proof.text: *Step 5 (part (a), 'if').* Let $\mathcal F$ be quasi-coherent, $U$ affine, $R=\mathcal O_X(U)$, and suppose $\mathcal F(U)$ is generated over $R$ by $m_1,\dots,m_n$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. By Step 3 the sections $m_1,\dots,m_n$ generate $\mathcal F|_U$, i.e. $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_U$, $e_i\mapsto m_i$, is surjective; so $\mathcal F|_U$ is of finite type [pqf-def-coherent] (the neighbourhood $U$ serves for every point). (Stacks 01PB states only the converse in its proof; this direction is the exactness of $\widetilde{\ }$ applied to $R^n\twoheadrightarrow M$.)

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PB (lemma-finite-type-module), line 2093, direction 'M finite implies finite type'

proof.text: *Step 6 (part (a), 'only if').* Suppose $\mathcal F|_U$ is of finite type; put $M=\mathcal F(U)$. Work on $X_U=\operatorname{Spec}R$ via $g$ (Step 1), where $\mathcal F|_{X_U}$ is quasi-coherent with global sections $M$ and the counit $\widetilde M\to\mathcal F|_{X_U}$ is an isomorphism [lem-weil-pbc-affine-tilde-gamma-adjunction](3). Let $x\in\operatorname{Spec}R$. By Step 1 there are an open $W\ni x$ and sections $s_1,\dots,s_n\in\mathcal F(W)$ generating $\mathcal F|_W$. The principal opens $D(r)$ form a basis of the Zariski topology (the complement of $V(I)$ is $\bigcup_{r\in I}D(r)$), so $x\in D(r)\subseteq W$ for some $r\in R$, and the restrictions $s_i|_{D(r)}$ generate $\mathcal F|_{D(r)}$ (restrict the local expressions $t|_{W_k}=\sum f_is_i|_{W_k}$ to $W_k\cap D(r)$). $D(r)$ is an affine open of $\operatorname{Spec}R$, the image of the open immersion $\operatorname{Spec}R_r\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion], with $\mathcal O(D(r))=R_r$ and $\mathcal F(D(r))\cong\widetilde M(D(r))=M_r$ as $R_r$-modules [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] (the case $N=R$ for the structure sheaf, $N=M$ for $\widetilde M$) [def-weil-pbc-module-localization-away]. By Step 3 (for the scheme $\operatorname{Spec}R$, the quasi-coherent module $\mathcal F|_{X_U}$ and the affine open $D(r)$) $M_r=\sum_iR_r\,s_i|_{D(r)}$ is a finitely generated $R_r$-module. The opens $D(r)$ obtained in this way for all $x$ cover $\operatorname{Spec}R$, which is quasi-compact, so finitely many $D(r_1),\dots,D(r_k)$ cover it and then $(r_1,\dots,r_k)=R$ [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact](i),(iii). Since every $M_{r_j}$ is finitely generated over $R_{r_j}$, $M$ is a finitely generated $R$-module [lem-weil-pbc-module-finite-of-localization-span] (Algebra 00EO(2)).

proof.text: *Step 7 (part (b), 'if').* Suppose $M=\mathcal F(U)$ is finitely presented: there is an exact sequence $R^m\xrightarrow{v}R^n\xrightarrow{u}M\to0$ (take generators $m_i=u(e_i)$ and let $v$ send the basis of $R^m$ to generators of the finitely generated kernel). Let $\varphi_u:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_U$ be given by the sections $u(e_i)\in M$ and $\varphi_v:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}$ by the sections $v(e_j)\in R^n=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n})$ (Step 1). The composite $\varphi_u\varphi_v$ is given by the sections $u(v(e_j))=0$, so it is $0$ (Step 1, uniqueness). Let $q:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to C=\operatorname{Coker}\varphi_v$; by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-cokernel-image] (on the scheme $U$) $C$ is quasi-coherent, $\operatorname{Im}\varphi_v=\ker q$, and $q_U$ is the quotient map $R^n\to R^n/v(R^m)=C(U)$. By the universal property of the cokernel there is a unique $\beta:C\to\mathcal F|_U$ with $\beta q=\varphi_u$; on $U$-sections $\beta_U:R^n/v(R^m)\to M$ is the map induced by $u$, bijective by exactness. By Step 2(i) $\beta$ is an isomorphism. Hence $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus m}\xrightarrow{\varphi_v}\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\xrightarrow{\varphi_u}\mathcal F|_U\to0$ is isomorphic to the cokernel sequence of $\varphi_v$ and is exact, so $\mathcal F|_U$ is of finite presentation (the neighbourhood $U$ serves for every point). (Stacks 01PC states only the converse in its proof; this direction is the right exactness of $\widetilde{\ }$.)

source.place: Properties, Lemma 01PC (lemma-finite-presentation-module), line 2113, direction 'M finitely presented implies finite presentation'

proof.text: *Step 8 (part (b), 'only if').* Suppose $\mathcal F|_U$ is of finite presentation. Then it is of finite type (a presentation contains a surjection $\mathcal O_W^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_W$), so $M=\mathcal F(U)$ is finitely generated by Step 6; choose $u:R^n\to M$ surjective. By Step 3 the sections $u(e_i)$ generate $\mathcal F|_U$, i.e. $\varphi_u:\mathcal O_U^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_U$ is surjective. Let $\mathcal K=\operatorname{Ker}\varphi_u$ ($V\mapsto\ker\varphi_{u,V}$): it is quasi-coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-quasi-coherent-module-kernel] (on the scheme $U$; $\varphi_u$ is a map between quasi-coherent modules by Step 1), and $\mathcal K(U)=\ker(\varphi_{u,U})=\ker u$ since $\varphi_{u,U}=u$ (Step 1). By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-presentation-kernel-surjection-finite-type] (Modules 01BP(1), on the ringed space $U$) $\mathcal K$ is of finite type. By Step 6 applied to the quasi-coherent $\mathcal K$ on the scheme $U$ and its affine open $U$, $\ker u=\mathcal K(U)$ is a finitely generated $R$-module. So $M\cong R^n/\ker u$ with $\ker u$ finitely generated: $M$ is finitely presented.

source.place: Properties, proof of Lemma 01PC (lemma-finite-presentation-module): 'By Lemma 01PB M is a finite R-module. Choose a surjection R^n → M with kernel K ... By Modules, Lemma 01BP we see that K~ is a finite type O_X-module. Hence by Lemma 01PB again K is a finite R-module.' (Stacks' 0 → K~ → O^n → M~ → 0 by the exactness of tilde, Schemes 01HV, is replaced by the kernel lemma)

proof.text: *Step 9 (part (c)).* Let $X=\bigcup_jU_j$ be an affine open covering with each $\mathcal F(U_j)$ finitely generated over $\mathcal O_X(U_j)$. By (a) (Step 5) each $\mathcal F|_{U_j}$ is of finite type: every point $x\in U_j$ has an open neighbourhood $W\subseteq U_j$ with a surjection $\mathcal O_W^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_W$, which is the condition of [pqf-def-coherent] for $\mathcal F$ at $x$; so $\mathcal F$ is of finite type. If $\mathcal F$ is of finite type and $U$ is any affine open, then $\mathcal F|_U$ is of finite type: for $x\in U$ with a surjection $\mathcal O_W^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_W$, its restriction to $W\cap U$ is still a surjection of sheaves (surjectivity is a local condition on sections over smaller opens); so $\mathcal F(U)$ is finitely generated by (a) (Step 6). Likewise if $\mathcal F$ is of finite presentation, restricting a presentation $\mathcal O_W^{\oplus m}\to\mathcal O_W^{\oplus n}\to\mathcal F|_W\to0$ to $W\cap U$ gives a presentation (restriction to an open preserves cokernels [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-open-immersion-colimits](1)), so $\mathcal F|_U$ is of finite presentation and $\mathcal F(U)$ is finitely presented by (b) (Step 8). (Stacks: finite type and finite presentation are local properties by their Definitions 01B5, 01BN; the remark before 01PB.)
